data.name: Airport Fire Department - The Simulation
data.detailed_description:
Fire can be a friend, but also a merciless foe. Nowhere else is the danger greater than at a modern airport with thousands of travellers and highly flammable kerosene.

The risks are extremely high, and so are the demands put on the elite team of the airport fire department! Even routine operations like defueling aircraft can become dangerous. A small incident can turn into a raging inferno!

Move out with your team and experience tense missions. As a member of the airport fire department, you and your team extinguish massive aircraft fires and beat a path through the flickering flames. Drive all kinds of fire-fighting vehicles and put out conflagrations with the mounted fire monitors. Combat localized fires with extinguishers and everything you can find in your equipment. Vanquish the indomitable flames!

Your team is counting on you. Don't let them down!

FEATURES

  • Realistic models of fire-fighting vehicles
  • Over 20 km² of airport grounds for a wide range of missions and hours and hours of fun
  • Numerous flammable items
  • Detailed vitality system for information about your own fitness

reviews.review:
Airport Fire Department – The Simulation, developed by VIS-Games and published by United Independent Entertainment, explores one of the most specialized branches of firefighting by placing players in charge of emergency response operations at a large commercial airport. Instead of the familiar urban fires found in many emergency simulators, this title shifts its focus toward aviation incidents where burning aircraft, fuel storage areas, terminals, and airport infrastructure present unique dangers. The concept alone gives the game a distinctive identity, offering a setting that few firefighting games attempt to recreate while emphasizing the responsibilities and risks faced by airport rescue crews.

The gameplay centers on responding to emergency dispatches using a fleet of airport firefighting vehicles built to tackle large-scale aviation fires. Players must drive these specialized trucks across a sprawling airport environment before deploying high-capacity water cannons to contain dangerous blazes. Certain situations also require leaving the vehicle to extinguish smaller fires with handheld equipment, creating a balance between vehicle operation and on-foot firefighting. The large airport serves as more than a backdrop, providing numerous locations where emergencies can unfold and reinforcing the feeling of working within an active transportation hub where disasters can occur without warning.

A major strength of the simulation is its emphasis on hazardous environments. Aviation fuel, explosive materials, and rapidly spreading fires create scenarios that demand careful planning instead of reckless action. Players are encouraged to position their vehicles strategically, control the spread of flames, and manage emergencies before they escalate into larger catastrophes. The inclusion of firefighter vitality introduces another layer of realism, reminding players that emergency responders must also monitor their own condition while operating in dangerous situations. Although these mechanics remain fairly straightforward compared to modern simulators, they successfully capture the importance of discipline and situational awareness during rescue operations.

As expected from a title originally released years ago, the presentation reflects its age. Vehicle models remain reasonably detailed, particularly the airport fire engines that form the centerpiece of the experience, while the airport itself offers an impressive sense of scale. However, environmental textures, character animations, lighting, and visual effects are noticeably dated by today's standards. Fire and smoke effects effectively communicate the urgency of emergencies, even if they lack the realism and visual intensity found in newer firefighting simulations. Players who appreciate older simulation games will likely find the graphics functional enough to support the gameplay despite their technical limitations.

The overall pacing favors realism over excitement. Missions encourage patience, methodical decision-making, and careful use of equipment rather than constant action. While this measured approach suits the simulation genre, the objective structure can become repetitive after extended play since most scenarios revolve around extinguishing fires in different sections of the airport. The expansive map and variety of emergency locations help reduce this repetition, but they cannot entirely mask the relatively limited mission diversity. Nevertheless, players specifically interested in emergency services and airport rescue operations will likely appreciate the game's commitment to its niche rather than expecting an action-heavy experience.

Airport Fire Department – The Simulation remains an interesting entry for fans of specialized emergency response games. Its authentic airport setting, dedicated firefighting vehicles, and focus on aviation-related disasters help distinguish it from more conventional firefighting simulators. Although its aging visuals, repetitive mission flow, and modest gameplay depth prevent it from competing with newer releases, it still delivers a respectable simulation of an often-overlooked profession. Those with an interest in airport operations, rescue services, or classic simulation games should find enough value in its unique premise to overlook its technical shortcomings.

Rating: 5/10
